title: Parrot probe: safe request duplication pipeline with tenant-aware sampling and spend fencing
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement a production-grade request duplication pipeline (codename: Parrot) that safely replays a sampled subset of live requests to candidate models without impacting tenant quotas or incurring uncontrolled cost. Parrot must provide: tenant isolation, dynamic sampling, spend fencing with soft/hard caps, latency and correctness observability, and automated rollback triggers when divergence or error thresholds are exceeded. This ticket covers the end-to-end design, a conservative phased rollout, and an automation hook for aborting duplication when cost or quality SLOs are violated.
acceptance_criteria: Parrot can duplicate requests to a candidate model with per-tenant sampling rates configurable via runtime flags
Duplication runs under a bounded budget: soft alert at 60% of budget, hard stop at 100% with automated drain policy
Requests duplicated by Parrot are tagged and routed through a tenant-scoped sandbox so they do not affect production quotas or caching behavior
Telemetry tracks token-cost delta, tail latency delta, response divergence rate, 5xx regression, and per-tenant spend; dashboards and alerts created
A canary rollout strategy allows opt-in subsets (routes/customers) to receive 100% duplication while global default is sampled
Automatic rollback action exists: if divergence-rate > 2% OR 99th latency delta > 200ms OR weekly duplicate spend projected to exceed budget by >20%, stop duplication and notify owners
E2E tests simulate noisy tenants, high-traffic customers, and failure modes (candidate model 503s, increased token inflation) and pass in CI
design_notes: We will avoid plumbing duplication into the main request path by introducing a lightweight non-blocking enqueue to Parrot's async router. Dupes are annotated with a stable fingerprint (method+path+major-prompt-hash+user-id-salt) to allow deterministic sampling and idempotent replay. Sandbox semantics: duplicated requests must bypass shared KV caches (use per-sandbox cache namespace) and not consume production rate-limiter tokens. Spend accounting: a separate metering pipeline aggregates tokens consumed by dupes, and a budget controller enforces tenant-level caps. For low-latency safety, synchronous duplication is forbidden; responses from candidate models do not impact the user-facing response. Privacy/PII: before replay we apply redaction rules from the common redaction service and mark replays as non-logged where required by tenant policy.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Core plumbing - async duplication enqueue, fingerprint hashing, per-tenant sampling config, tagging headers (1 week)
Phase 2: Sandbox isolation - per-tenant cache namespace, replay identity header, quota-exemption layer, and KMS-aware request scrubber (2 weeks)
Phase 3: Cost metering & budget controller - token counting for duplicates, soft/hard thresholds, alerting hooks, and automatic stop API (1.5 weeks)
Phase 4: Observability - dashboards for token delta, divergence, latency delta, per-tenant spend; synthetic probes for regressions (1 week)
Phase 5: Safety automation - rollback triggers, circuit-breaker state machine, and runbook integrations (1 week)
Phase 6: Canary rollout & docs - opt-in labels, UI flags, runbook, SDK examples and integration tests (1 week)
